title.narrative: Enhancing Sudan Right to Education, EIE

description.narrative:
The conflict that erupted on 15 April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) continues to inflict dire consequences on civilians, exacerbating the protracted economic troubles and pre-existing conflicts in the country. Thousands of people were killed and injured, millions of people fleeing their homes in search of safety, both inside Sudan and across its borders, and millions grappling with a lack of access to food, water, and other basic services. OCHA reported that since the start of the conflict, the magnitude of IDPs and refugees is on the rise - over 1 million people were forced to cross into neighbouring countries and more than 4.2 million people (845,779 Households) have been displaced to (3,929) locations across all 18 states. Approximately 25 million people, roughly half of Sudan’s population, are now vulnerable and need humanitarian assistance and protection through the end of 2023 . An estimated 19 million children in Sudan are out of school, some 6.5 million lost access to school due to the conflict, and 10,400 schools shuttered in conflict-affected areas , and 171 schools are serving as emergency shelters for the displaced population , exposing children to dangers including recruitment into armed groups, and sexual violence. The number of displaced, separated, or unaccompanied children will continue to increase as families flee. This emphasizes the need to support education to ensure its continuity and ensure that Sudanese children equitably access school and have sufficient psychosocial support in safe and child-friendly learning spaces. This calls for not only coordinated action at the national level but also a harmonized approach at the regional level. The Minister of Education (MoE) recently issued a directive for the resumption of all academic activities in all government, private, and non-governmental schools, and higher education institutions where security conditions permit, following months’ full closure of education institutions throughout the country. As requested by the MoE to support school reopening, education partners, including UNESCO, are seeking ways to ensure access and equity to safe education, and alternative learning options for learners, especially IDPs, to mitigate learning deficits and ensure continuity of learning. A key member of the Local Education Group (LEG) in Sudan, UNESCO Khartoum leads critical education portfolios and works closely with key national stakeholders as well as development and humanitarian partners to make sure learning continues under all circumstances. In addition to leading technical fields, UNESCO has recently taken on board the role of LEG Coordinating Agency in the framework of GPE, whereby the organization has been entrusted with strengthening the coordination of education actors through the identification of emergency priorities and harmonizing donor financing around them. In the last meeting of the LEG, held on November 27, 2023, it was agreed among members to develop a Transitional Education Plan for the period 2024 to 2026 (TEP 2024-26). Sudan has been in war situation starting April 2023, national capacities in Education in Emergency is quite limited as Sudan was not in such situation before. Lack of appropriate data on the current status of schools, teacher and students is not helping the planning process for all Sudan educational partners.
UNESCO Khartoum plans to conduct a study on the current status of educational institutions and teachers to support the Local Education Group (LEG) better plan for 2024-2025. UNESCO Khartoum, been the Coordinating Agency for the LEG has the mandate and the authorization from the LEG to conduct data collection study on the current status of educational institutions. Khartoum office intends to use this project to complete the missing data. In addition, Khartoum office would like to bridge the gap in education senior officials on Education In Emergency through training program involving HQ colleagues from EiE.
Outcome No. 1: Sudan Educational System is enhanced in Planning of Education In Emergencies for 2024 – 2026 and better coordination among Local Education Group. Output 1: Sudan National Transitional Education Plan for 2024 - 26 is developed and approved among Local Education Group. Activity 1.1: National and International Experts are identified and recruited to support the development of the TEP 2024-26. Activity 1.2: Sudanese Local Education Group coordination and planning is improved.
Output 2: Sudan National Capacities are increased in planning and monitoring of Education in Emergencies. Activity 2.1: National capacities of the LEG and education officials are developed in EiE planning and monitoring.
Rational and Implementation Strategy: To achieve the set Outcome and Output UNESCO as a coordinating Agency for the LEG will work with national and international partners and with the support of 4 experts to identify the priorities that the TEP should focus on, this will be through in person and online discussions and workshops. This work will be supported by GPE (promised 100k US$ and UNESCO HQ provided 50k US$). After the priorities are set the project will work with all LEG members and experts to develop initiatives for each of the identified priorities. The project will also identify several scenarios to accommodate the political instability of the current war situation learning from Yamen, Syria and other UNESCO experience around the world. The project will also develop a monitoring and evaluation plan, this will make the focus of UNESCO intervention in the TEP and the LEG. The project will also train national educational officials and LEG members on EiE planning and monitoring through online workshop.
